answer.rationale: Finance mandates 18% cost cut, contract does not auto-renew in 14 days, and low-cost vendor quote already meets the mandate alone. Memory c2 confirms a prior primary switch to the same low-cost vendor 'cut unit cost sharply' with quick onboarding and accurate invoicing. Verifying c2 confirms this is not new ground, not a leap, and not on the leading edge of uncertainty — it's a reapplication of a recently archived, high-signal outcome. That materially de-risks the decision. Memory c4 confirms that incumbent renegotiation can recover real margin but does not mention hitting an 18% mandate or structural unit-cost parity. Verifying c4 rules out the strongest alternative — whether incumbent could match the low-cost quote on price plus terms. If verification shows incumbent cannot meet the mandate, the choice is obvious. If they can, I still have to weigh c4's margin recovery against c2's larger unit-cost reduction, and 14 days is too short to run a serious parallel negotiation with the line running at 94% with no buffer. Note: c6 (multi-year incumbent) could lower cost further, but multi-year lock-in raises switching risk if c2's edge is structural; I prefer to switch now and consider multi-year with the new primary at next review. Intended action is switch_primary_vendor at a small guarded scale rather than full volume migration, so the line stays protected and the second review can confirm invoicing accuracy and on-time delivery before scaling. Will not exceed the two-memory verification budget.
